parts.name: Battery Pack
parts.description: 4 × AA alkaline holder with chemistry-shaped discharge, internal resistance and runtime depletion.

paramHelp.voltage: Scales the chemistry profile; a fresh 4×AA pack is above its 6 V nominal rating.
paramHelp.rInternal: Fresh-pack reference. The simulator raises resistance as charge falls and in cold ambient conditions.
paramHelp.capacityAh: Reference-drain capacity used for coulomb counting. High real-world drain reduces usable alkaline capacity.
paramHelp.charge: Initial state of charge. It decreases with simulated current draw; editing it resets the runtime battery state.

parts.applications: Primary DC rail for simple breadboard projects. Connect pos to the top red rail and neg to the top blue (GND) rail; bridge to the bottom rails when both banks are used.

electrical_specs.notes: 4×AA alkaline model. Chemistry OCV is ~6.4 V fresh, then follows a piecewise discharge curve; internal resistance rises with depletion and cold. Capacity is coulomb-counted from a 2.5 Ah moderate-drain reference. Recovery, self-discharge, aging, cell imbalance and self-heating are not modelled.

bom.polarityNotes: Red wire is positive (+), black wire is negative (GND). Connect red to the positive power rail.
bom.ratings: 6 V nominal (4×1.5 V), 500–1000 mA typical
bom.beginnerDescription: A plastic holder for four AA batteries that provides around 5-6 V to power your breadboard circuit.

parts.name: Bench PSU
parts.description: Adjustable DC bench power supply.

paramHelp.iLimit: Output current is capped at this limit.

parts.applications: Use when the project needs a voltage other than 5V or a current limit (3.3V logic, 9V buzzers, 12V relays). Pos to red rail, neg to blue rail.

electrical_specs.notes: Adjustable DC bench supply, voltage and current-limit settable.

bom.beginnerDescription: A lab bench power supply that lets you dial in any DC voltage and set a current limit — it is bench equipment you already own, not a per-project purchase.

parts.name: Pulse Generator
parts.description: Signal generator: rectangular pulsed voltage.

paramHelp.per: Time between pulses. Set to 0 for one pulse, which returns to the low level and does not repeat.

parts.applications: Single-shot or repeating pulse generator. Drive logic inputs that need a deterministic edge for testing.

electrical_specs.notes: Piecewise-linear pulse source. A positive period repeats the pulse; period=0 is a one-shot that returns to v1 after its fall time.

bom.beginnerDescription: A bench instrument that produces adjustable rectangular pulses for testing logic circuits — bench equipment, not a per-project part.

parts.name: Clock Generator
parts.description: Signal generator: square-wave clock output.
parts.applications: Fixed 1 kHz square-wave clock for driving counter/shift-register/sequential-logic inputs without building a 555 astable.

bom.beginnerDescription: A bench instrument that outputs a fixed square-wave clock for driving counters and shift registers — bench equipment, not a per-project part.

parts.name: Signal Generator
parts.description: A bench function generator producing DC, sine, square, pulse, triangle, ramp, piecewise-linear, or noise signals.

paramHelp.amplitude: Peak volts for deterministic waveforms. In noise mode, this is the Gaussian 1-sigma RMS voltage.
paramHelp.offset: Shifts the whole waveform up or down.

parts.applications: Use this when you need a versatile bench signal source that can produce DC bias, sinusoidal AC, square/pulse clocks, triangle/ramp sweeps, arbitrary piecewise-linear waveforms, or Gaussian noise for testing analog and mixed-signal circuits.

electrical_specs.notes: V(t) = offset + amplitude x unit(t). For noise, unit(t) is deterministic zero-mean Gaussian noise updated at 10 kSa/s and held between updates; amplitude is its 1-sigma RMS voltage and the zero-order hold has 5 kHz one-sided equivalent noise bandwidth. rSource is the series output resistance (50 Ω bench default). PWL points are specified as absolute volts using t:v,t:v pairs.

bom.beginnerDescription: A bench instrument that can produce sine, square, triangle, and other waveforms for testing circuits — bench equipment, not a per-project part.

parts.name: Resistor
parts.description: Ohmic resistor (configurable resistance).

paramHelp.resistance: Nominal resistance at the reference temperature. Identified quarter-watt parts heat from I²R dissipation, but body temperature does not change resistance because temperature coefficient is not modelled.
paramHelp.tolerance: Manufacturing spread used by tolerance analysis; it does not represent temperature coefficient or long-term drift.

parts.applications: Use for current limiting (LED in series), pull-up/pull-down (to VCC or GND on a digital input), voltage division, and biasing. For a typical red LED at 5V, 330Ω limits current to ~10 mA.

thermal.r_theta_condition: Derived from a 0.25 W P70 derating curve reaching a 155 °C film hot spot.
assumptions: The 8 s one-pole time constant is a teaching-model assumption.
Lead length, PCB copper, resistor technology, and airflow can materially change the thermal path.

electrical_specs.notes: Quarter-watt axial-film reference: 0.25 W through 70 °C ambient, then linear derating to 0 W at a 155 °C film limit. For an identified resistor, solved I²R loss drives the persistent one-pole body temperature and ambient-adjusted power allowance. Temperature is reported but does not change resistance because temperature coefficient is not modelled.

bom.beginnerDescription: A small cylindrical component with coloured stripes that limits how much current flows through a wire — the most commonly used part in electronics.

parts.name: Capacitor
parts.description: Capacitor with configurable series resistance and dielectric leakage.

paramHelp.esr: Equivalent series resistance dissipates energy and limits charge/discharge current. Set to 0 for an ideal series path.
paramHelp.leakageResistance: Resistance across the capacitor terminals. Lower values make stored charge decay faster; set to 0 to disable leakage.
paramHelp.style: Electrolytic caps are polarized - the striped leg is negative and goes to the lower voltage.

parts.applications: Decoupling (100 nF ceramic across VCC/GND of every IC, within 2 columns of the supply pins), timing (in RC networks with 555), bulk filtering (electrolytic 10–100 µF across power rails), AC coupling.

electrical_specs.notes: `style` selects the body. The transient model is ideal capacitance in series with `esr`, plus terminal-parallel `leakageResistance`. Defaults are representative, not a substitute for a chosen part's datasheet. Capacitance tolerance, ESR frequency/temperature dependence, dielectric absorption, voltage coefficient, polarity damage, and breakdown are not modelled.

commonSubstitutions: electrolytic capacitor (if value >= 1 uF and polarity observed)
bom.beginnerDescription: A tiny disk or cylinder that stores a small burst of electrical charge and filters out noise — a 100 nF ceramic is the standard decoupling cap placed near every IC.

paramHelp.vf: Voltage lost across the diode while conducting.

parts.applications: One-way current. Use for reverse-polarity protection, freewheeling across inductive loads (relays, motors), and rectifying AC.

bom.polarityNotes: Cathode (K) is marked with a silver band. Current flows from anode (A) to cathode only.
bom.ratings: 1 A, 1000 V PIV
bom.beginnerDescription: A small glass or plastic cylinder that allows current to flow in only one direction — useful for protecting circuits against reversed batteries.

parts.name: Zener Diode
parts.description: Zener diode — voltage regulation via reverse breakdown.

paramHelp.vz: Conducts in reverse above this - used to clamp or regulate.

parts.applications: Reverse-biased voltage reference / clamp. The `vz` param sets the breakdown voltage.

electrical_specs.notes: Reverse breakdown voltage set by `vz` param (e.g. 5.1V). iz_knee is the knee current at the rated vz (default 5 mA). vz is not varied by Monte Carlo v1 — the engine does not apply vz via a params override.

bom.polarityNotes: Cathode (K) is marked with a band. In regulation use, cathode connects to the positive rail; forward direction is the same as a regular diode.
bom.ratings: 5.1 V zener voltage, 1 W
bom.beginnerDescription: A special diode that, when reverse-biased past its rated voltage, clamps the voltage at that level — handy for making a simple 5 V reference.

parts.name: TVS Diode
parts.description: Transient Voltage Suppressor — clamps fast voltage spikes by entering reverse breakdown.

paramHelp.vbr: Clamps spikes above this to protect the circuit.

parts.applications: ESD and transient spike protection on signal or power lines. The `vbr` param sets the standoff/breakdown voltage. Set `bidirectional` to 1 for AC-line or bipolar signal protection.

electrical_specs.notes: Breakdown voltage set by `vbr` param (default 6.8 V). bidirectional=0 (default) for unidirectional, 1 for symmetric bidirectional clamping. For reverse-overvoltage, the vr_max check is suppressed below vbr — normal operation.

bom.genericName: 6.8 V 400 mW TVS diode (P6KE6.8 or equivalent)
bom.polarityNotes: Cathode (K) marked with a band. For unidirectional use cathode toward the positive rail. Bidirectional TVS has no functional polarity.
bom.ratings: 6.8 V standoff, 400 mW
bom.beginnerDescription: A fast-response protection diode that clamps voltage spikes — place it across a signal line to absorb ESD or inductive kickback.

parts.name: Schottky Diode
parts.description: Schottky barrier diode — low forward voltage drop.

paramHelp.vf: Lower than a normal diode - that is the point of a Schottky.

parts.applications: Low forward-drop one-way diode (~0.3V). Use where 0.7V silicon drop is too high — power rails on small batteries, fast switching.

bom.polarityNotes: Cathode (K) is marked with a band. Same orientation convention as a standard rectifier diode.
bom.beginnerDescription: A diode with an unusually low voltage drop (~0.3 V instead of 0.7 V), useful where you need one-way current flow without losing too much voltage.

parts.name: Inductor
parts.description: Inductor with configurable winding resistance and lumped core loss.

paramHelp.dcr: DC resistance of the winding wire. It limits current and dissipates copper loss; set to 0 for an ideal winding.
paramHelp.coreLossResistance: Terminal-parallel lumped approximation of magnetic core loss. Lower values increase loss; set to 0 to disable it.

parts.applications: Stores energy in a magnetic field. RF filtering, switching converters, and tuned circuits. Resists changes in current.

electrical_specs.notes: The transient model is ideal inductance in series with winding `dcr`, plus terminal-parallel `coreLossResistance`. Defaults represent a generic 1 mH axial part; use its datasheet values when known. Saturation, nonlinear permeability, hysteresis, frequency-dependent loss, skin effect, self-capacitance, and thermal drift are not modelled.

bom.beginnerDescription: A coil of wire that resists sudden changes in current — used in filters and switching power supplies.

parts.description: Red-coloured light emitting diode. Vf ≈ 1.8 V.

paramHelp.vf: Nominal rated-current forward voltage for this colour. Identified package self-heating feeds the nonlinear junction law; optical efficacy and the overload-failure threshold do not change with temperature.

parts.applications: Indicator. Always use a series resistor — for a red LED at 5V supply, 330Ω limits current to ~10 mA. Anode to + side, cathode to GND side.

thermal.r_theta_condition: 5 mm through-hole reference on FR4 with at least 16 mm² pad area per lead.
assumptions: The 2 s one-pole time constant is a teaching-model assumption.

No reversible thermal shutdown is claimed.

parts.name: NPN Transistor
parts.description: Generic NPN BJT (Ebers-Moll transport model with forward Early effect).

paramHelp.betaF: How many times the base current is amplified.
paramHelp.earlyVoltage: Forward Early voltage VA. Lower values give more collector-current change with VCE; set to 0 to disable.

bom.ratings: Ic max 600 mA, beta ~100, Vce 30 V
bom.beginnerDescription: A three-legged amplifier/switch — apply a small current to the base pin to control a larger current flowing through the collector and emitter.

parts.name: N-Channel MOSFET

paramHelp.vto: The gate voltage where it starts conducting.
paramHelp.cgs: Fixed lumped gate-source capacitance used for transient gate charging.
paramHelp.cgd: Fixed lumped gate-drain (Miller) capacitance used for transient coupling.

parts.name: CD4511
parts.description: BCD-to-7-segment latch/decoder/driver with push-pull active-high outputs (16-pin DIP, CMOS-4000).
parts.applications: BCD-to-7-segment decoder for common-cathode displays. Outputs are push-pull active-HIGH — connect directly to common-cathode display with a series resistor per segment to VCC. LE LOW: outputs follow BCD inputs (transparent). LE HIGH: outputs hold last value. /LT LOW forces all segments ON. /BL LOW forces all segments OFF. Tie /LT and /BL HIGH, LE LOW for basic transparent operation.

electrical_specs.notes: CRITICAL DIFFERENCE from 74LS47: outputs are active-HIGH push-pull (not open-collector). Use with common-CATHODE displays. BCD inputs 10-15 produce ALL SEGMENTS BLANK (not partial glyphs like 74LS47). Digit 6: no top bar (a off), no segment b. Digit 9: no bottom bar (d off). Source: TI CD4511B datasheet, SCHS021.

parts.name: CD4060
parts.description: 14-stage binary ripple counter with built-in oscillator (16-pin DIP, CMOS-4000).
parts.applications: 14-stage ripple counter with internal oscillator. RC oscillator (Nexperia HEF4060B Rev. 11, Section 11): connect Rt (resistor) from RTC (pin 10) to CLK/RS (pin 11), and Ct (capacitor) from CTC (pin 9) to CLK/RS (pin 11); f approx 1/(2.3*Rt*Ct); recommend Rt >= 10 kOhm, Ct >= 100 pF. For external clock: drive CLK/RS (pin 11) directly, leave CTC/RTC unconnected. Counter advances on FALLING edge of CLK/RS. RESET HIGH clears counter and inhibits oscillation. Q4 first HIGH after 8 internal clocks. Available external outputs: Q4-Q10, Q12-Q14 (Q1-Q3, Q11 are internal only). Oscillation emerges from the adaptive transient solve; use solver health and scope effective-rate provenance to assess fast setups (Rt=47k, Ct=47nF gives f~196 Hz).

electrical_specs.notes: Available outputs with external pins: Q4-Q10, Q12-Q14. Internal stages with NO pins: Q1-Q3, Q11. Oscillator: Rt from RTC (pin 10) to CLK/RS (pin 11), Ct from CTC (pin 9) to CLK/RS (pin 11); f = 1/(2.3 * Rt * Ct); recommend Rt >= 10 kOhm, Ct >= 100 pF. Counter advances on falling edge of CLK/RS (pin 11). CTC (pin 9) = NOT(CLK/RS); RTC (pin 10) = NOT(CTC) = in-phase with CLK/RS. Oscillation emerges from the adaptive transient solve; there is no fixed 50 us engine clock. Solver health and scope effective-rate provenance disclose whether a fast setup is adequately resolved. Source: TI CD4060B datasheet, SCHS007; pin map cross-referenced to Nexperia HEF4060B Rev. 11, Table 2.

parts.name: 9 V Battery
parts.description: PP3/6LR61 9 V alkaline battery with snap connector. 1.5 Ω internal resistance models real voltage sag under load.

paramHelp.rInternal: Fresh-battery reference. The simulator raises resistance as charge falls and in cold ambient conditions.
paramHelp.capacityAh: Low-drain reference used for coulomb counting; a real PP3 delivers less capacity at high current.
paramHelp.charge: Initial state of charge. It decreases with simulated current draw; editing it resets the runtime battery state.

parts.applications: 9 V supply for Arduino, small amplifiers, buzzers and wireless modules. Higher voltage than 4×AA lets regulators run closer to their nominal drop-out. Connect snap connector red (+) to the red power rail and black (−) to the blue GND rail. Set initial charge below 100% to start with a partially discharged cell.

electrical_specs.notes: PP3 / 6LR61 alkaline. Runtime charge is coulomb-counted from a 0.55 Ah low-drain reference. Chemistry OCV and internal resistance change with charge; resistance also rises in cold ambient conditions. High-current rate-capacity loss, recovery, self-discharge, aging and self-heating are not modelled.

bom.genericName: 9 V PP3 alkaline battery with snap connector
bom.polarityNotes: Red wire is positive (+), black wire is negative (GND). Connect to matching snap connector on the battery.
bom.ratings: 9 V nominal, 500–600 mAh typical (alkaline)
bom.beginnerDescription: A single rectangular 9 V battery with a snap connector — clip it on and connect the leads to your breadboard power rails.

parts.name: CR2032 Coin Cell
parts.description: 3 V lithium coin cell (CR2032). 10 Ω internal resistance limits peak current, modelling the high impedance of a coin cell.

paramHelp.rInternal: Fresh-cell reference. The simulator raises resistance as charge falls and in cold ambient conditions.
paramHelp.capacityAh: 15 kΩ / 21 °C reference capacity used for coulomb counting; pulse loads deliver less usable capacity.
paramHelp.charge: Initial state of charge. It decreases with simulated current draw; editing it resets the runtime battery state.

parts.applications: Backup power for RTC modules, low-power microcontrollers, key fobs and small sensor boards. The high internal resistance naturally limits short-circuit current, protecting the cell. Use when a coin cell holder is in circuit — not a general-purpose high-current source.

electrical_specs.notes: CR2032 lithium coin cell. Runtime charge is coulomb-counted from a 235 mAh, 15 kΩ / 21 °C reference. Chemistry OCV and internal resistance change with charge; resistance rises strongly in cold ambient conditions. Pulse-load capacity loss, recovery, self-discharge, aging and self-heating are not modelled.

bom.polarityNotes: Positive (+) is the flat top face; negative (−) is the ribbed bottom. Mount in a CR2032 coin-cell holder.
bom.ratings: 3 V nominal, 210–240 mAh, max continuous draw ~5 mA
bom.beginnerDescription: A small, flat button battery that powers low-energy circuits like clocks, small sensors, and key fobs.

parts.name: DC-DC Buck Converter
parts.description: Non-isolated step-down (buck) switching converter module. Converts a higher input voltage to a regulated 5 V output at up to 2 A with 85% efficiency; IN− and OUT− share one internal return.

paramHelp.vdropout: Typical averaged input-to-output headroom at maximum duty cycle. The output cannot exceed Vin minus this loss.

parts.applications: Step down 7–35 V (e.g. 12 V wall adapter or LiPo pack) to a stable lower-voltage rail for Arduino or logic circuits. Efficiency ~85% means significantly less heat than a linear regulator at high voltage drops. Connect IN+ to the input supply and OUT+ to the load; IN− and OUT− are the same internal return and do not provide isolation. Set vout below Vin with enough dropout headroom; this buck model cannot boost.

electrical_specs.notes: Behavioural non-isolated buck model: IN− and OUT− are one internal return. Within the declared 7–35 V input range, the output regulates at vout (CV), current-limits at iLimit (CC), or follows the averaged maximum-duty ceiling Vout=Vin−vdropout (default 1.5 V). It cannot boost. Present-solve input draw satisfies Iin=Pout/(eta×Vin), including load and regime changes. Below UVLO, above maximum input, or with reversed polarity, it is OFF. Switching ripple and control-loop transients are omitted.

bom.genericName: Step-down DC-DC converter module (e.g. MP1584, LM2596)
bom.polarityNotes: IN+ to positive supply, OUT+ to regulated output; IN− and OUT− share one internal GND return (non-isolated).
bom.ratings: Vin 7–35 V, adjustable lower Vout with about 1.5 V modelled dropout headroom, Iout up to 2–3 A typical
bom.beginnerDescription: A small green module that converts a higher voltage (like 12 V) down to a lower one (like 5 V) very efficiently — much cooler than a linear regulator.

parts.name: 5 V SPDT Relay
parts.description: Electromechanical single-pole double-throw relay. A coil (coil_a/coil_b) magnetically actuates a contact arm that switches COM between NO (normally-open) and NC (normally-closed). Add a flyback diode anti-parallel across the coil to suppress the inductive kick when the driver turns off.

paramHelp.vPull: Coil voltage that closes the contacts.

parts.applications: Switch high-voltage or high-current loads (motors, lamps, AC mains) from a low-power microcontroller output. Drive the coil through a transistor (NPN: collector to coil_a, emitter to GND, coil_b to +5 V) and always add a 1N4001 flyback diode anti-parallel across the coil to protect the driver from the inductive kick. Energised: COM connects to NO. De-energised: COM connects to NC.

electrical_specs.notes: Coil modelled as series R+L (backward-Euler Norton companion). Contact switching uses hysteresis on coil voltage: pull-in when |V_coil| >= vPull, drop-out when |V_coil| < vDrop. Always add a flyback diode across the coil; see the missing-flyback diagnostic.

bom.polarityNotes: Coil polarity does not matter (relay responds to |V_coil|). COM/NO/NC contacts are isolated from the coil.
bom.ratings: Coil: 5 VDC, 70 Ω (≈71 mA). Contacts: 10 A / 250 VAC or 10 A / 30 VDC.
bom.beginnerDescription: An electrically-controlled switch. Apply voltage to the coil and the contact arm clicks over, connecting COM to the NO terminal instead of NC.

parts.name: ULN2003A
parts.description: 7-channel Darlington sink array (DIP-16). Each channel accepts a logic input and sinks up to 500 mA through an open-collector NPN Darlington pair. TTL/CMOS compatible inputs (Vih ≥ 2.5 V). Internal catch diodes on each output; connect COM to the load supply to suppress inductive kicks without an external flyback diode.
parts.applications: Drive LEDs, relays, motors, solenoids and other inductive or resistive loads from low-current logic outputs (MCU GPIO, 74xx gates). Each channel handles up to 500 mA. Wire IN to the logic driver, OUT to the load (with a pull-up to supply), GND to circuit GND, and COM to the load supply rail so the internal catch diodes suppress inductive spikes without an external flyback diode.

electrical_specs.notes: No VCC pin. Inputs referenced to GND. Output is open-collector sink only; external pull-up or load required for high state. Internal catch diodes from each OUT to COM are electrically modelled and clamp inductive spikes when COM is tied to the load supply rail. Vce_sat is simplified as R_on=5 ohm (approximately 1 V at 200 mA).

bom.polarityNotes: Pin 1 at notch/dot end. IN1-IN7 on left, OUT7-OUT1 on right (reversed order). GND pin 8, COM pin 9.
bom.orientationNotes: Place with notch facing left; pin 1 at top-left.
bom.ratings: 50 V output (Vce max), 500 mA per channel, 2.5 W package total
bom.beginnerDescription: A 16-pin chip that lets a microcontroller drive 7 separate high-current loads (like relays or motors) without burning out its output pins.

parts.name: ULN2803A
parts.description: 8-channel Darlington sink array (DIP-18). Same as ULN2003A but with 8 channels and CMOS/TTL-compatible inputs. Inputs 1-8 on left, COM and OUT8-OUT1 on right. Ideal for driving 8-bit parallel loads from a microcontroller port or shift register.
parts.applications: Drive 8 independent high-current loads from an 8-bit MCU port or 74HC595 shift register. Perfect for driving eight relays, stepper-motor phases, or LED arrays simultaneously. Wire each IN to the corresponding logic output, each OUT to the corresponding load (with pull-up to supply), GND to circuit GND, and COM to the load supply so internal catch diodes handle inductive spikes.

electrical_specs.notes: 8-channel variant of ULN2003A. DIP-18. All electrical characteristics are identical to ULN2003A per channel, including electrically modelled OUT-to-COM catch diodes. Inputs are CMOS/TTL compatible (Vih min 2.5 V, Vil max 1.5 V per ULN2803A datasheet Table 1).

bom.polarityNotes: Pin 1 at notch/dot end. IN1-IN8 on left, OUT8-OUT1 on right (reversed). GND pin 9, COM pin 10.
bom.orientationNotes: Place with notch facing left; pin 1 at top-left.
bom.ratings: 50 V output (Vce max), 500 mA per channel, 2.5 W package total
bom.beginnerDescription: An 18-pin chip that lets a microcontroller's 8-bit port drive eight high-current loads (relays, motors, LED arrays) without burning out the GPIO pins.

parts.name: Active Buzzer
parts.description: Active piezo/magnetic buzzer with internal oscillator. Apply a DC voltage (2–5 V) to make it sound — no external frequency source needed. Electrically a resistive load (~16–32 Ω coil). The internal oscillator runs at a fixed frequency (typically 2 kHz) when the DC level exceeds ~1.5 V.

paramHelp.type: Active buzzers beep on plain DC power; passive ones need a tone signal.

parts.applications: Generate audible alerts or feedback tones. For active buzzers: wire + to the logic output (or transistor collector), − to GND. For passive buzzers: drive with a square wave (PWM) at audio frequency (200 Hz–8 kHz). Use a series resistor or transistor driver to protect GPIO pins. The sounding state is reported in the simulator readout.

electrical_specs.notes: Active buzzer: DC threshold 1.5 V for internal oscillator to run. Passive buzzer: must be driven with an AC/PWM signal; frequency reported from zero-crossing detection. Both types modelled as a fixed resistor (resistance param, default 32 Ω). No audio synthesis — sounding state and detected frequency only.

bom.polarityNotes: Positive pin is longer (anode). Usually marked with + on the label. Reverse polarity will not damage most buzzers but the oscillator will not run.
bom.ratings: 2–5 V operating, typically 30–90 mA at 5 V
bom.beginnerDescription: A small round module that makes a continuous beeping sound whenever you apply 5 V to it — no extra circuitry needed.

parts.name: Passive Buzzer
parts.description: Passive piezo buzzer without internal oscillator. Must be driven with an AC or PWM signal at audio frequency (200 Hz–8 kHz). Electrically a resistive load (~16–32 Ω). The pitch is determined by the drive frequency; use with a clock generator or PWM output.

paramHelp.type: Active buzzers beep on plain DC power; passive ones need a tone signal.

parts.applications: Generate variable-pitch tones for music, MIDI-like output, or user feedback. Drive with a 50% duty-cycle square wave from a clock_gen or Arduino PWM pin. The simulator detects the frequency and reports it. Use a small transistor driver or ULN2003 channel to protect the digital output.

electrical_specs.notes: Passive buzzer: requires AC/PWM drive signal. Frequency detected via zero-crossing counting. Sounding when detected frequency > 0 Hz. Same resistor model as active buzzer (resistance param). No audio synthesis.

bom.polarityNotes: Polarity usually not critical for passive piezo buzzers. Check datasheet of specific part.
bom.ratings: Typically 3–5 V, 30 mA, 85–100 dB at 10 cm
bom.beginnerDescription: A passive buzzer makes sound at whatever frequency you drive it at — great for playing simple tunes from a microcontroller.

parts.name: 8 Ohm Speaker
parts.description: Small 8 Ω permanent-magnet speaker for breadboard audio circuits. The voice coil is modelled as a resistive load (8 Ω nominal). Signal-present is detected when the terminal voltage has a peak-to-peak amplitude above 50 mV over a 5 ms window. No audio synthesis — readout only.
parts.applications: Output audio from a circuit driven by an LM386 audio amplifier, Arduino with PWM, or similar signal source. Connect + to the amplifier output and − to ground. For best results use a coupling capacitor to block the DC bias. The simulator shows a 'signal present' indicator when voltage variation is detected across the speaker terminals.

electrical_specs.notes: Voice coil modelled as pure resistance (8 Ω default). AC reactance of the coil inductance is ignored at audio frequencies for this simplified model. Signal-present detection uses a 5 ms sliding window; peak-to-peak amplitude ≥ 50 mV registers as sounding.

bom.genericName: 8 ohm small speaker (28 mm or 36 mm diameter)
bom.polarityNotes: For DC-coupled circuits observe + terminal polarity. For AC-coupled (capacitor-coupled) circuits polarity is less critical.
bom.ratings: 8 Ω, 0.5–1 W typical breadboard speaker
bom.beginnerDescription: A small speaker that turns electrical signals into sound — pair it with an amplifier chip like the LM386 to hear audio from your circuit.

parts.name: L293D Dual H-Bridge
parts.description: Quadruple half-H driver capable of driving two DC motors bidirectionally or four independent loads. Four independent half-bridges (OUT1–OUT4) are enabled in pairs: EN12 enables channels 1+2, EN34 enables 3+4. A separate motor supply (VCC2/VM, up to 36 V) drives the output stage while VCC1 (4.5–7 V) powers the logic. Internal recirculating clamp diodes on every output suppress inductive kickback from motor windings when VM is supplied — no external flyback diode needed across motor terminals.
parts.applications: Bidirectional DC motor control, stepper motor drive (half-step / full-step), solenoid and relay driving from MCU GPIO. Forward: EN high, IN1 high, IN2 low. Reverse: EN high, IN1 low, IN2 high. Coast: EN low. Wire VCC1 to 5 V logic supply and VCC2 to the motor supply (up to 36 V). GND pins must all be wired to circuit GND.

electrical_specs.notes: VCC1 (logic, 4.5–7 V) and VCC2/VM (motor rail, 4.5–36 V) are separate supplies. Output stage R_on = 2 Ω per side (1.4 V total drop at 1 A across both output transistors). Internal clamp diodes on each output pin recirculate inductive kickback to VM — suppress missing-flyback when VM is wired. io_max 0.6 A continuous per channel (1.2 A peak).

bom.polarityNotes: VCC1 pin 16 to logic supply, VCC2 pin 8 to motor supply. All four GND pins (4, 5, 12, 13) must be wired to GND.
bom.ratings: VCC1 4.5–7 V logic, VCC2 up to 36 V motor, 0.6 A continuous / 1.2 A peak per channel
bom.beginnerDescription: A 16-pin IC that lets a microcontroller drive two small DC motors forward and backward — the classic motor-driver chip for robot projects.

parts.name: TB6612FNG Dual H-Bridge
parts.description: Dual full-H-bridge motor driver module (modelled as a 16-pin DIP-compatible breakout). Two independent H-bridge channels (A and B) each support forward, reverse, brake, and coast modes via two direction inputs plus a PWM input. A shared STBY pin puts both channels into hi-Z standby. Internal freewheeling diodes on every output suppress inductive kickback when VM is supplied.
parts.applications: Bidirectional control of two DC motors from a microcontroller. Channel A: drive PWMA high, AIN1=1/AIN2=0 for forward, AIN1=0/AIN2=1 for reverse, AIN1=AIN2=1 for brake, AIN1=AIN2=0 for coast. Same for channel B with PWMB/BIN1/BIN2. STBY must be high for any output to be active. Wire VCC to 3.3–5 V logic supply and VM to the motor rail (2.5–13.5 V).

electrical_specs.notes: VCC (logic, 2.7–5.5 V) and VM (motor rail, 2.5–13.5 V) are separate supplies. R_on = 2 Ω per output side (simplified; real device specifies on-resistance as Vce_sat ~0.5 V at 1 A). PWM duty-cycle averaging for speed control is a Wave 7 motor-dynamics feature — in this model PWM is treated as a binary enable: HIGH=active, LOW=coast. Internal freewheeling diodes suppress inductive kickback when VM is wired. io_max 1.2 A continuous per channel.

bom.polarityNotes: VCC pin to logic supply (3.3–5 V), VM to motor supply (up to 13.5 V), all GND pins to circuit GND. STBY must be pulled HIGH to enable outputs.
bom.ratings: VM 2.5–13.5 V, 1.2 A continuous / 3.2 A peak per channel
bom.beginnerDescription: A motor-driver breakout that lets a microcontroller run two DC motors in both directions — popular with the Arduino ecosystem for small robots.

parts.name: DC Motor
parts.description: Generic brushed DC motor. Modelled as a series R+L winding (windingR, windingL) with a back-EMF source proportional to rotor speed (Vbemf = Ke × omega). Torque is generated by winding current (Tm = Kt × i). Rotor dynamics: J × dω/dt = Kt×i − b×ω − loadTorque. Use an H-bridge driver (L293D, TB6612) for bidirectional control; a bare transistor switch requires a flyback diode across the motor terminals.

paramHelp.loadTorque: Braking torque the motor must overcome.

parts.applications: Bidirectional DC motor control via H-bridge (L293D, TB6612). For forward rotation connect M+ to H-bridge OUT_A, M− to OUT_B; reverse the H-bridge drive signals for reverse rotation. A bare transistor switch requires a flyback diode anti-parallel across M+/M− to suppress the inductive kick when the transistor turns off. The rotor speed (omega, rad/s) and RPM are reported in the simulator readout.

electrical_specs.notes: Winding modelled as series R+L with backward-Euler Norton companion. Back-EMF = Ke × omega opposes applied voltage (motor convention), causing current to decrease as speed rises. Stall current = V / windingR (omega=0). No-load steady-state: omega = (V − R × i_ss) / Ke, i_ss = b × omega_ss / Kt. Rotor dynamics use forward-Euler (stable when h << J/b). omega is a simulator readout and back-EMF driver only — no mechanical coupling to external loads. windingR and windingL must be > 0; inertia must be > 0.

bom.genericName: Generic brushed DC motor (e.g. FA-130, N20, JGA25-370)
bom.polarityNotes: M+ (m1) to positive drive voltage or H-bridge output; M− (m2) to negative drive or GND. Reversing polarity reverses rotation direction.
bom.ratings: Operating voltage: 3–12 V (model-dependent). Stall current at default R=5Ω and V=6V: 1.2 A. Always use an H-bridge driver or a transistor with flyback diode for switching.
bom.beginnerDescription: A small electric motor that spins when voltage is applied. Speed depends on voltage; direction depends on polarity. Needs a driver circuit (like L293D) to control from a microcontroller.

parts.name: Hobby Servo (SG90)
parts.description: PWM-controlled rotary position actuator. A 1–2 ms HIGH pulse updates a target between 0° and 180°; the shaft then moves toward that target at a finite, supply-scaled speed. The default idle load draws about 15 mA at 5 V.

paramHelp.idleR: Equivalent idle load across V+ and GND. At 5 V, 330 Ω draws about 15 mA.
paramHelp.movingCurrent: Teaching reference at the nominal supply while the shaft is travelling. It becomes an equivalent load, not a stall or torque model.
paramHelp.maxSpeedDegPerSecond: No-load travel rate at the nominal supply. 600°/s equals 0.1 s per 60°.
paramHelp.nominalVoltage: Supply voltage at which speed and moving-current references are defined.
paramHelp.minimumOperatingVoltage: Below this solved supply, the shaft stops but retains its decoded target.
paramHelp.minPulseMs: HIGH-pulse width that commands the minimum target angle.
paramHelp.maxPulseMs: HIGH-pulse width that commands the maximum target angle.
paramHelp.minAngle: Lower mechanical travel limit and target for minPulseMs.
paramHelp.maxAngle: Upper mechanical travel limit and target for maxPulseMs.

parts.applications: Pan-tilt mounts, robotic arms, RC vehicles and latch mechanisms. Drive Signal with an Arduino Servo library or correctly timed 50 Hz pulses; analogWrite alone does not generate a conventional servo command. Use a 4.5–6 V supply with adequate current capacity and connect its ground to the controller ground. A separate supply is recommended for multiple servos or loaded motion.

electrical_specs.notes: Signal is a truly high-impedance physical input; no 1 MΩ pull-down is present. Solver regularisation of a floating net is numerical only and does not represent a physical load. A falling PWM edge decodes targetAngle from the 1–2 ms pulse, while angle reports the actual shaft position. Actual angle travels without overshoot at 600°/s at 4.8 V and scales linearly with solved supply, giving 625°/s at 5 V. Below the 4.5 V model brownout threshold, velocity becomes zero while targetAngle is retained. At rest, V+ to GND uses idleR=330 Ω. While moving, the 150 mA at 4.8 V teaching assumption becomes a 32 Ω equivalent load. Torque, stall mechanics/current limiting, acceleration, backlash, control hunting, gearbox compliance and heating are not modelled.

bom.polarityNotes: Connector is polarised: signal (orange/yellow) leftmost, power (red) centre, GND (brown/black) rightmost. Do not reverse.
bom.ratings: Model supply 4.5–6 V; speed 600°/s at 4.8 V; idle load about 15 mA at 5 V; moving-load assumption 150 mA at 4.8 V. Typical real stall current can approach 700 mA and stall torque about 1.8 kg·cm, neither is simulated.
bom.beginnerDescription: A small plastic motor with gears that turns to a specific angle when you send it a PWM signal. Use the Arduino Servo library to control it easily.

parts.name: Bipolar Stepper Motor (NEMA 17)
parts.description: 4-wire bipolar stepper motor with two independent coils (A and B). Energise the coils in the 4-phase full-step sequence to advance the shaft one step at a time. Default: 200 steps/rev (1.8°/step). Drive with an H-bridge such as L293D or TB6612. Unipolar/ULN2003 5-wire steppers are not modelled in this wave.

paramHelp.stepsPerRev: 200 steps = 1.8° per step, the most common.

parts.applications: CNC axes, 3D printer carriages, camera sliders, precision positioning. Drive with an L293D (wires OUT1→a1, OUT2→a2, OUT3→b1, OUT4→b2) or TB6612 (AO1→a1, AO2→a2, BO1→b1, BO2→b2). Cycle the 4-phase full-step sequence: (A+,B+), (A-,B+), (A-,B-), (A+,B-). Each phase transition = 1 step = 1.8° for a 200-step motor. Add a flyback diode across each coil when using bare transistor drivers.

electrical_specs.notes: Each coil is a series R+L Norton companion (backward-Euler, same as relay coil). No back-EMF in v1. Step detection uses committed current sign post-solve: signA = sign(iA), signB = sign(iB), deadband ±1 mA. Phase sequence: (A+,B+)=0, (A-,B+)=1, (A-,B-)=2, (A+,B-)=3. Sequential phase advance +1 (mod 4) increments position; −1 (mod 4) decrements. Non-sequential jump holds. Stepper coils are inductive — flyback diagnostic fires for bare-transistor drive; suppressed by L293D/TB6612 with VM powered. Unipolar/ULN2003 variant deferred.

bom.polarityNotes: Coil A: a1=A+, a2=A−. Coil B: b1=B+, b2=B−. Reversing a coil reverses direction. Identify coils with a multimeter (continuity between a1/a2 and between b1/b2).
bom.ratings: Typical: 12 V, 0.4–1.7 A per coil (model-dependent). Hold torque: 40–60 N·cm. Default model: coilR=10 Ω, coilL=10 mH, 200 steps/rev.
bom.beginnerDescription: A motor that moves one precise step at a time instead of spinning freely. Great for robots and printers where you need to know exactly how far something has moved.

parts.name: MAX7219 8x8 LED Matrix
parts.description: SPI-controlled 8x8 LED matrix driver module. The MAX7219 accepts 16-bit serial frames (register address + data) over a 3-wire SPI-compatible interface (DIN/CLK/CS). Each step() decodes sub-step MCU pin events for accurate multi-frame replay, or falls back to sampled levels for discrete drive. Registers: digit/row 0x01-0x08 store the 8 row bytes; 0x0A sets intensity (0-15); 0x0B sets scan limit (0-7 rows active); 0x0C enables/disables (1=normal, 0=shutdown); 0x0F = display test (all LEDs on). Single-device only in v1 (no daisy-chain DOUT). Decode mode raw only (0x00; BCD mode not simulated).
parts.applications: Drive an 8x8 red LED matrix from a microcontroller using only 3 GPIO pins. Wire DIN to a data output pin, CLK to a clock pin, and CS (chip-select/load) to a third GPIO. Send register 0x0C=0x01 to exit shutdown, 0x0B=0x07 to enable all 8 rows, 0x0A=0x08 for mid-intensity, then write rows 0x01-0x08 with the desired pixel patterns. Bit 7 of each byte = leftmost column; bit 0 = rightmost column.

electrical_specs.notes: Supply modelled as a 150-ohm behavioural load (~33 mA at 5 V) representing a representative lit-matrix draw. Per-LED current accuracy is out of scope for v1; the teaching focus is the decoded pixel pattern. DIN, CLK and CS are high-impedance logic inputs with no invented physical pull-down; an undriven input follows the simulator's disclosed floating-input decision model. Single-device only: DOUT daisy-chain is not modelled. Decode mode must be 0x00 (raw segment bits); BCD mode (0x09) is stored but not rendered.

bom.polarityNotes: VCC to 5 V, GND to circuit GND. DIN to MCU data-out, CLK to MCU clock-out, CS (chip-select) to MCU GPIO. CS idles HIGH; pull LOW to start a frame, pulse CLK 16 times, pull CS HIGH to latch.
bom.ratings: VCC 4.0-5.5 V. Supply current up to 330 mA with all LEDs on at max intensity. Each LED segment max 40 mA; limit with RSET resistor (module boards include one).
bom.beginnerDescription: A small module that lets you control 64 LEDs in an 8x8 grid using just 3 wires from your Arduino. Perfect for scrolling text, animations, and simple games.

parts.name: HD44780 16x2 LCD
parts.description: HD44780-compatible 16-character x 2-line character LCD module. Accepts 4-bit or 8-bit parallel interface via RS/RW/E control lines and D0-D7 data lines. Command subset simulated: clear (0x01), return home (0x02/0x03), entry mode set (0x04-0x07), display on/off (0x08-0x0F), function set (0x20-0x3F) for 4-bit/8-bit and 1-line/2-line selection, set CGRAM address (0x40-0x7F, data writes ignored in v1), set DDRAM address (0x80-0xFF). DDRAM address map: 0x00-0x0F = line 1, 0x40-0x4F = line 2 (only the first 16 positions of each 40-byte bank are visible). Cursor/display shift command (0x10-0x1F) accepted but not rendered. RW pin is sampled but read-back is not supported; tie RW to GND. No custom CGRAM glyphs in v1. ASCII 0x20-0x7E rendered; codes outside this range display as space.
parts.applications: Display text from a microcontroller with a familiar parallel interface. In 4-bit mode wire RS, RW, E, and D4-D7 from 4 Arduino GPIO pins (D0-D3 left unconnected). Send function-set 0x28 to enter 4-bit 2-line mode, then 0x0C for display-on, 0x01 to clear, 0x06 for entry mode, then write character ASCII bytes with RS=1. In 8-bit mode wire all 8 data lines. Tie RW to GND (write-only). VSS to circuit GND, VDD to 5 V. V0 sets contrast (connect to a 10 k pot wiper or tie to GND for max contrast). A/K are backlight anode/cathode (3.3 V via 47-100 ohm resistor typical).

electrical_specs.notes: Supply modelled as a 200-ohm behavioural load (~25 mA at 5 V) representing logic + backlight draw. RS/RW/E/D0-D7 are high-impedance logic inputs with no invented physical pull-down; an undriven input follows the simulator's disclosed floating-input decision model. RW read-back is not supported in v1; tie RW to GND. Custom CGRAM glyphs (codes 0x00-0x07) display as space. Katakana ROM region (0xA0-0xFF) not simulated. HD44780 ROM quirks (0x5C=yen, 0x7E/0x7F=arrows) treated as ASCII. 4-bit and 8-bit modes both supported via function-set DL bit.

bom.polarityNotes: VSS to GND, VDD to 5 V. RW to GND (write-only). RS and E to MCU GPIO. In 4-bit mode: D4-D7 to MCU GPIO, D0-D3 unconnected. V0 to pot wiper for contrast. A/K for backlight via current-limiting resistor.
bom.ratings: VDD 4.5-5.5 V. Logic ICC ~1-2 mA. Backlight LED ~20-60 mA at 3.3 V (module-dependent). HD44780 controller: CMOS 0-70 degC operating range.
bom.beginnerDescription: The classic 16-character, 2-line text display used in countless beginner Arduino projects. Shows custom messages, sensor readings, and menus using a simple parallel bus.

parts.name: Ultrasonic Distance Sensor (HC-SR04)
parts.description: Ultrasonic time-of-flight distance sensor. Fires a short ultrasonic pulse from one transducer and times how long the echo takes to return on the other, so a microcontroller can compute range. Wide-supply model (3.0-5.5 V) so 3.3 V boards (micro:bit, RP2040) and 5 V boards (Arduino) can both drive it directly.
parts.applications: Obstacle avoidance and range-finding for robotics, parking-sensor demos, and water-level or proximity gauges. Wire VCC to a 3.0-5.5 V rail (5 V recommended for a classic HC-SR04; 3.3 V direct-wire is a real, purchasable HC-SR04P/clone behaviour), TRIG to a digital output pin, and ECHO to a digital input pin. Fire a HIGH pulse on TRIG for at least 10 microseconds, then measure the ECHO HIGH pulse width (pulseIn on Arduino, machine.time_pulse_us on MicroPython) and convert to distance at 58.0 microseconds per centimetre.

electrical_specs.notes: Wide-supply model: functional 3.0-5.5 V, matching HC-SR04P and common 3.3 V-tolerant clones. A classic HC-SR04 module is commonly specified 5 V-only, so treat direct 3.3 V operation as clone-dependent on real hardware. Below 3.0 V (VCC-GND) the sensor is inert: ECHO is forced low/hi-Z and TRIG pulses are ignored. TRIG is a 1 MOhm pulldown input, armed by a rising edge; the sensor schedules an echo on the following falling edge (re-triggering while an echo is pending/active is ignored, matching real module behaviour). ECHO timing: rises at trigFall + 250 microseconds, then falls 58.0 microseconds/cm x distanceCm later, or after a 38 millisecond timeout when noEcho (out-of-range) is set. ECHO drives push-pull to the sensor's own committed VCC through the house 50 ohm gate output resistance.

bom.genericName: HC-SR04 ultrasonic distance sensor module (or HC-SR04P wide-supply variant)
bom.polarityNotes: 4-pin header, not keyed by shape — wire VCC/TRIG/ECHO/GND exactly per silkscreen; reversing VCC and GND can damage the module.
bom.ratings: VCC 3.0-5.5 V (HC-SR04P / 3.3 V-tolerant clones) or 5 V (classic HC-SR04). Quiescent current ~2 mA. Range 2-400 cm, resolution ~0.3 cm, beam angle ~15 degrees.
bom.beginnerDescription: A distance sensor that pings an ultrasonic 'chirp' out of one speaker-like transducer and listens for the echo on the other, timing the round trip so your code can measure how far away an object is.
